subject: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls from today's discovery call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@fintechco.com>; Priya Kaur <pri.kaur@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>; Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls from today's discovery call

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the FintechCo requirements for request/response logging, headers/trace IDs, and PII redaction: 

Recap (what we heard)
- You need request/response logging for troubleshooting and audit, but must exclude or redact any PII fields (names, SSNs, account numbers) and any routing headers that could be used for user re-identification.
- Retention policy: logs kept for 90 days searchable, with a 1-year cold archive for audit-only access.
- Data residency: production inference must run in us-east-1; logs may remain in us-east-1 or move to FintechCo-owned S3 in your AWS account.
- Trace IDs & correlation headers: keep for observability, but strip/mask user-identifying metadata before any logs leave your VPC or Redwood-managed storage.

Clarifications from our side (what Redwood can do)
- Redwood supports configurable request/response logging levels (none|minimal|full). We can redact at ingestion using field-based rules and regex masks. We also support masking headers and dropping trace IDs from persisted logs when configured.
- For request/response payloads we offer: prefix-based KV cache masking, token-level redaction rules, and a post-processing redaction step that can be run before logs are stored or forwarded.
- We can push logs to your S3 (customer-owned) via an encrypted delivery connector (KMS/HSM), or store them in Redwood-managed buckets with role-restricted access and audit logs.

Open questions / asks for FintechCo
1) Can you share the initial list of fields you consider PII + regex examples? (e.g. SSN pattern, account id formats)
2) Is FintechCo comfortable with trace IDs being present in ephemeral logs for 7 days but removed from persisted logs?
3) Do you want us to generate a sample redaction config (YAML) that your security team can review?

Proposed next steps
- I'll send a sample redaction config and SOC2 evidence summary by EOD tomorrow. (attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, logging-redaction-config-sample.yaml)
- Lauren (cc'd) will follow up with a short demo of the redaction workflow / masking rules early next week.
- Priya / Sam to share the PII field list and retention confirmation.

If this matches your understanding, we'll turn these into a short mutual action plan and include timing for a security review.

Thanks again — great conversation.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive 
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
- logging-redaction-config-sample.yaml (text, 6KB)
From: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kaur <pri.kaur@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:31:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls from today's discovery call

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. A few quick answers inline: 

Open questions:
1) PII list: we'll share a CSV tonight with the fields. Top items: customer_full_name, dob, ssn (format 3-2-4), payment_account_id (alphanumeric, 16 chars), last4_card (4 digits). Will add examples/regex.
2) Trace IDs: yes, ephemeral (7 days) is fine but must be removed from persisted logs. For audit we can keep correlation IDs in the cold archive with restricted access if they are stored in a customer-owned bucket.
3) Yes please send a sample redaction YAML for our security team to review.

Two additional asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a short runbook describing the redaction failure modes and how incident response would work if a redaction rule missed something?
- We need clarification on whether headers like "X-User-Context" could contain identifiable values; if so, we need guidance on pattern matching and recommended header strip/mask rules.

We'll upload the PII list and examples to the Drive link you shared. Priya and I will also pull in our security engineer for the next review.

Sam
Head of Platform Engineering
FintechCo
sam.nguyen@fintechco.com | +1 212-555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls from today's discovery call

Sam / Priya —

Appreciate the quick confirmations and the PII list you'll upload. Next items from our side: 

1) Attached are the redaction config sample and SOC2 summary as promised. The YAML includes example rules for SSN (regex), account ids (prefix-based), and header strip/mask entries for X-User-Context and X-Trace-ID.
2) Lauren will run the short demo of the redaction pipeline on Monday 2026-03-09 at 10:00am ET — calendar invite to follow. That demo will cover: rule authoring, previewing masked examples, failure-mode alerts, and how to route un-redacted snippets to a secure review queue.
3) Dev will prepare a 1-page runbook that outlines: detection of redaction misses, escalation path, and how we support log reprocessing and guarded deletion in customer-owned S3. Expect that doc on Friday 2026-03-06.

If you'd like, we can enable a temporary sandbox in us-east-1 with sample traffic so you can validate masking rules against your real request examples without touching production. Let us know if you want the sandbox and we'll provision it under the FTCO-POC project.

Action items summary:
- FintechCo: upload PII CSV + examples to Drive (Sam/Priya) — due 2026-03-05.
- Redwood: send runbook (Dev) — due 2026-03-06; demo (Lauren) — 2026-03-09; redaction YAML + SOC2 summary (attached) — done.

Thanks — we'll follow up with the calendar invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
